newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's Unibanco makes NYSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Unibanco makes NYSE debut.

text.p: Brazil's Unibanco Group SA made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday in heavy trade that shot it near the top of the most-active list.
In late morning Unibanco's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were at 34-1/8 after being priced at 33-3/4. Volume was 4.9 million ADRs, making Unibanco the second-most-active share on the exchange.
Unibanco, the third-biggest private bank in Brazil, undertook the offering on behalf of Brazil's Central Bank.

The sale is part of a program to clear up the debts of failed Banco Nacional, which remains under Central Bank administration. Unibanco deposited shares with the Central Bank as part of a goodwill payment during its buyout of Banco Nacional's healthy portion in 1995.

Unibanco is offering 28.5 million units outside Brazil as part of a global offering, with 20.6 million being offered in the United States. Each unit represents one preferred share in Unibanco and one preferred share in Unibanco holding. Both shares are non-voting.
Unibanco is the first Brazilian bank and the third Brazilian company to list on the New York Stock Exchange.
